name: Hackman’s Five Conditions for Team Effectiveness
diagnostic: Diffuse team boundaries where individuals belong to multiple conflicting squads, shifting sprint targets resulting in cynicism, and inadequate CI/CD tooling or access privileges preventing work execution.

script.label: Structural Boundary Delineation
script.text: "Current sprint throughput indicates an ambiguous distribution of team capacity. We will delineate our boundary conditions. The team requires explicit definition: who is dedicated exclusively to this deliverable, what non-negotiable metric dictates success for this release, and what external dependencies lack operational support from engineering management?"

audit: Does every contributor name one squad that owns their capacity?
Did the sprint goal stay unchanged across the fourteen-day interval?
auditFull: Do 100% of team contributors identify a single primary squad owner for their capacity?
Has the sprint roadmap established a quantitative goal that remained invariant over the fourteen-day interval?
foundation: Formulated by J. Richard Hackman (2002), this framework asserts that high team performance does not stem from charismatic leadership, but from five structural conditions: a real team with stable boundaries, a compelling direction, an enabling structure, a supportive organizational context, and expert coaching. Hackman’s empirical studies across corporate and governmental task forces revealed that these systemic conditions account for up to 60% of the variance in team outcomes.

origin.title: Leading Teams: Setting the Stage for Great Performances
